correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite simple G, initial observations are originals N_G[R] union L and leaves R union L. Only L\R can force initially unobserved originals U. A legal sequence yields distinct agent-target edges whose ordered biadjacency matrix is triangular with diagonal 1, hence uniquely restricted. Conversely a uniquely restricted saturating matching has an acyclic alternating-exchange digraph and a sink permits sequential forces. For forest bases B(A,U) is acyclic, so Hall and target-saturating matching coincide; the 128-state rooted recurrence stores Boolean existence for parent-edge matching and counts selection patterns rather than matching witnesses. Direct independently implemented brute-forcing and matching checks agree on all 16,932 labeled instances with at most four base vertices. The full theorem is proven by these combinatorial arguments, not finite verification.
